scenes.tts: The worm has two killers, a brake, and a protein that releases it. Does a mammal use the same parts?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Same Parts in Us. Worm pathway on the left: EGL-1, CED-9, CED-4, CED-3.
scenes.narration: The worm has two killers, a brake, and a protein that releases it. Does a mammal use the same parts?

scenes.tts: Cloning the worm genes gave the answer.
scenes.visual: Gene sequences scroll beside each worm protein.
scenes.narration: Cloning the worm genes gave the answer.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-three, ced-three turned out to resemble a mammalian protease.
scenes.caption: In 1993, ced-3 turned out to resemble a mammalian protease.
scenes.visual: Credit: 1993. CED-3 linked to a mammalian protease.
scenes.narration: In 1993, ced-3 turned out to resemble a mammalian protease.

scenes.tts: That protease belongs to a family later named caspases.
scenes.visual: Label: caspases.
scenes.narration: That protease belongs to a family later named caspases.

scenes.tts: Caspases cut with a cysteine in their active site.
scenes.visual: Caspase-3 structure (1PAU) with the active-site cysteine highlighted.
scenes.narration: Caspases cut with a cysteine in their active site.

scenes.tts: They cut just after an aspartate in their target.
scenes.visual: A bound peptide inhibitor in the pocket; its aspartate highlighted beside the cysteine.
scenes.narration: They cut just after an aspartate in their target.

scenes.tts: Caspases are made as inactive precursors.
scenes.visual: Inactive caspase shapes, folded shut.
scenes.narration: Caspases are made as inactive precursors.

scenes.tts: Initiator caspases switch on when they are gathered onto a platform.
scenes.visual: Initiators gather on a platform and light up. Label: initiator.
scenes.narration: Initiator caspases switch on when they are gathered onto a platform.

scenes.tts: They then cut and activate executioner caspases.
scenes.visual: Initiators cut executioners, which light up. Label: executioner.
scenes.narration: They then cut and activate executioner caspases.

scenes.tts: Executioners cut hundreds of cellular proteins, and take the cell apart.
scenes.visual: Executioners cut many protein shapes; the cell outline breaks up.
scenes.narration: Executioners cut hundreds of cellular proteins, and take the cell apart.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-four, ced-nine turned out to be a relative of human B C L two.
scenes.caption: In 1994, ced-9 turned out to be a relative of human Bcl-2.
scenes.visual: Credit: 1994. CED-9 linked to Bcl-2.
scenes.narration: In 1994, ced-9 turned out to be a relative of human Bcl-2.

scenes.tts: B C L two is a protein that keeps cells alive.
scenes.caption: Bcl-2 is a protein that keeps cells alive.
scenes.visual: Bcl-2 shown as a shield over a cell.
scenes.narration: Bcl-2 is a protein that keeps cells alive.

scenes.tts: It belongs to the B C L two family. Its members decide whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.
scenes.caption: It belongs to the BCL-2 family. Its members decide whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.
scenes.visual: A mitochondrion holding cytochrome c; BCL-2 family members at its surface.
scenes.narration: It belongs to the BCL-2 family. Its members decide whether mitochondria release cytochrome c.

scenes.tts: Some members protect. Others, such as Bax, promote death. The B H three only members, like E G L one, promote death too. That short domain is their only shared family feature.
scenes.caption: Some members protect. Others, such as Bax, promote death. The BH3-only members, like EGL-1, promote death too. That short domain is their only shared family feature.
scenes.visual: Family lineup in three groups: protectors such as Bcl-2; pro-death effectors Bax and Bak; pro-death BH3-only regulators such as Bim and EGL-1, each with only the BH3 segment marked.
scenes.narration: Some members protect. Others, such as Bax, promote death. The BH3-only members, like EGL-1, promote death too. That short domain is their only shared family feature.

scenes.tts: And ced-four proved related to a mammalian protein, Apaf one.
scenes.caption: And ced-4 proved related to a mammalian protein, Apaf-1.
scenes.visual: CED-4 linked to Apaf-1.
scenes.narration: And ced-4 proved related to a mammalian protein, Apaf-1.

scenes.tts: So each worm part has a mammalian counterpart. But read where the match fails, too.
scenes.visual: Worm-to-mammal table fills its first three columns, row by row.
scenes.narration: So each worm part has a mammalian counterpart. But read where the match fails, too.

scenes.tts: First, a question. Which mammalian part has no clear counterpart in the worm?
scenes.visual: Question card held over the table; the last row is blank.
scenes.narration: First, a question. Which mammalian part has no clear counterpart in the worm?

scenes.tts: Bax. It is a gate in the outer mitochondrial membrane. The worm has no clear counterpart.
scenes.visual: Last row fills: (none) in the worm column, Bax in the mammal column.
scenes.narration: Bax. It is a gate in the outer mitochondrial membrane. The worm has no clear counterpart.

scenes.tts: Now read where the match fails.
scenes.visual: The fourth column, 'where the match fails', starts to fill.
scenes.narration: Now read where the match fails.

scenes.tts: The worm brake holds ced-four directly. The mammalian brake guards the mitochondria.
scenes.caption: The worm brake holds CED-4 directly. The mammalian brake guards the mitochondria.
scenes.visual: Side by side: CED-9 holding CED-4; Bcl-2 guarding a mitochondrion.
scenes.narration: The worm brake holds CED-4 directly. The mammalian brake guards the mitochondria.

scenes.tts: Apaf one needs cytochrome c. There is no clear role for cytochrome c in worm apoptosis.
scenes.caption: Apaf-1 needs cytochrome c. There is no clear role for cytochrome c in worm apoptosis.
scenes.visual: Apaf-1 with cytochrome c; CED-4 alone, with a question mark where cytochrome c would be.
scenes.narration: Apaf-1 needs cytochrome c. There is no clear role for cytochrome c in worm apoptosis.

scenes.tts: E G L one resembles B H three only proteins, such as Bim, only in that domain.
scenes.caption: EGL-1 resembles BH3-only proteins, such as Bim, only in that domain.
scenes.visual: EGL-1 and Bim aligned; only the BH3 segment matches.
scenes.narration: EGL-1 resembles BH3-only proteins, such as Bim, only in that domain.

scenes.tts: So E G L one is best called a functional counterpart.
scenes.caption: So EGL-1 is best called a functional counterpart.
scenes.visual: Label: functional counterpart.
scenes.narration: So EGL-1 is best called a functional counterpart.

scenes.tts: And the worm's main caspase, ced-three, maps onto several mammalian caspases. Mammals split the initiator and executioner roles.
scenes.visual: CED-3 fans out to caspase-9 (initiator) and caspase-3 (executioner).
scenes.narration: And the worm's main caspase, CED-3, maps onto several mammalian caspases. Mammals split the initiator and executioner roles.
scenes.caption: And the worm's main caspase, CED-3, maps onto several mammalian caspases. Mammals split the initiator and executioner roles.

scenes.tts: In two thousand two, a Nobel Prize honoured discoveries concerning the genetic regulation of organ development and programmed cell death.
scenes.caption: In 2002, a Nobel Prize honoured discoveries concerning the genetic regulation of organ development and programmed cell death.
scenes.visual: Credit: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, 2002.
scenes.narration: In 2002, a Nobel Prize honoured discoveries concerning the genetic regulation of organ development and programmed cell death.

scenes.tts: Here is the first part of this lesson's one idea.
scenes.visual: Guiding idea card appears, one line visible.
scenes.narration: Here is the first part of this lesson's one idea.

scenes.tts: The killers are already built; a survival signal keeps brakes on them.
scenes.visual: End card line: the killers are already built; a survival signal keeps brakes on them.
scenes.narration: The killers are already built; a survival signal keeps brakes on them.
